All five are implemented in `problems.py`; names, signatures, and docstrings are untouched, stdlib only (`re`, `collections`).

- **`parse_duration`** — single anchored regex `(?:([0-9]+)h)?(?:([0-9]+)m)?(?:([0-9]+)s)?` requiring at least one group. This rejects out-of-order, duplicate, bare-unit, negative, whitespace, and trailing-garbage input in one shot; `[0-9]` rather than `\d` so non-ASCII digits don't slip through, and `\A…\Z` so a trailing newline isn't accepted. Non-string input raises `ValueError`, not `TypeError`.
- **`luhn_valid`** — strips spaces/hyphens, returns `False` on empty/non-digit/non-string rather than raising; `"0"` sums to 0 and passes.
- **`flatten`** — recursive walk building a fresh dict, so the input isn't mutated; empty sub-dicts contribute nothing since only leaves are written, and lists/`None` pass through as-is. Output preserves natural DFS key order.
- **`top_k_frequent`** — `Counter` plus `sorted(key=(-count, word))`, sliced to `k`; `k <= 0` short-circuits to `[]`, and slicing handles `k` beyond the distinct count.
- **`rolling_max`** — monotonic deque of indices, O(n) with each index pushed and popped once. `window <= 0` raises `ValueError`, `window > len(nums)` returns `[]`.

Verified against a throwaway suite (~90 cases, since deleted) covering every edge case the docstrings call out, plus a perf check: 300k elements with window 1000 in 0.115s, spot-checked against brute-force `max()`. All passed. Working tree has only the `problems.py` modification — no new files, no commits.
